title: M. leprae as the other famous mycobacterium
dek: Wikipedia's leprosy bacillus is not NTM in this teaching cut and not MTBC. It exists so TB graphs do not swallow Hansen's disease.
story: M. leprae on Wikipedia is an unculturable (on ordinary media) mycobacterium causing Hansen's disease. It shares genus trivia and some envelope chemistry with Mtb, and it shares neither NAATs nor WHO TB regimens.
This card is a boundary stone: TB knowledge graphs love to eat neighbouring mycobacteria. Leprae's diagnostic and treatment grammar is a different programme.
BCG has a messy, modest story in leprosy prevention on encyclopedia pages. That is not TPT for TB contacts.
deep: Phenolic glycolipid-1 serology and slit-skin smears are leprosy objects.
Armadillo reservoirs are trivia that do not belong in a pulmonary TB algorithm.
Genome reduction versus Mtb is a comparative-genomics pointer, not DST.
If a 'TB' WGS is leprae, the sample/label is the emergency.

visual.caption: Genus with three teaching buckets. Leprae is a named bucket, not a leftover NTM, not a TB lineage.
